question: Your team commits the project's .mcp.json so every developer on the customer support agent connects to the same backend MCP server. This server provides get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund and escalate_to_human, and it needs an API key for the billing system. Each developer has a personal key, and no secret may enter version control. How should you supply the key to the server?

options.text: Write the key directly into the committed .mcp.json and restrict repository access to members of the support team.
options.reason: This commits a secret to version control, which environment variable expansion in .mcp.json exists to avoid.

options.text: Move the whole server definition into each developer's ~/.claude.json and remove the shared server from the project configuration.
options.reason: User-level ~/.claude.json is for personal or experimental servers, while shared team tooling belongs in the project-level .mcp.json with environment variable expansion.

options.text: Store the key in the agent's system prompt, which is committed with the code, so the agent passes it to the tools.
options.reason: The key still ends up in committed files, so this fails the goal of credential management without committing secrets.

options.text: Reference the key in .mcp.json as ${BILLING_API_KEY} and have each developer set that environment variable on their own machine.
options.reason: Environment variable expansion in .mcp.json keeps the shared configuration in version control while each developer supplies a credential without committing a secret.
